topics: Latency corridor behavior and p99 spikes during cache cold-starts
Rollforward / fallback plan when Dedicated pool capacity constrained
Security controls: SSO, KMS, audit logs
Bench plan: 10k short sequences, KV warmup, token accounting
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-02
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: see metadata

[00:00] Santiago Ruiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Santiago from Redwood — glad to see the BlueWave crew. quick check: did everyone get the agenda i sent this morning?
[00:18] Ava Patel: yes, got it. thanks. we'll mostly want to walk through the creds handoff and then the bench numbers we ran overnight.
[00:30] Maya Chen: and i'll flag a couple of configuration tweaks we think will smooth the p99 spikes — some are kv cache warm-up related, some are batching windows.
[00:45] Tom Reynolds: cool, i'll jump in when we show the graphs, some of the numbers surprised us.
[00:52] Santiago: perfect. quick status: we uploaded the staging gateway playbook to the shared drive, there's a tiny script to create short-lived keys via the API — note the default TTL is 8 hours, you can increase if you want longer lived creds for CI.
[01:10] Priya Sharma: 8 hours is fine but for automation we need a token rotation path using your KMS. is that in the playbook?
[01:22] Santiago: good call — the playbook shows both the one-click and the KMS-backed flow; the KMS/HSM integration is in the private deployment doc but we can surface a minimal example for the staging gateway.
[01:38] Marcus Liu: will we get an IAM role example for the VPC peering side? our infra team needs the exact inbound port list.
[01:50] Eliot Park: yes, we included the minimal SG rules — port ranges and CIDR are in the snippet. i'll paste the snippet in chat after the call.
[02:05] Ava: awesome. okay bench recap: last night we ran a 2k request sample then a 10k run; the 2k looked fine, but the 10k shows periodic p99 spikes to ~620ms while p95 stayed around 180ms.
[02:23] Maya: that feels like a cache cold-start pattern — if many concurrent requests miss the prefix cache and force model kv loads you can see short windows of elevated latency. are you seeing correlation with new sessions?
[02:36] Tom: yes, a lot of our traffic has varied sequence length; some sessions spike to 1.8k tokens. i also saw that the spike moments line up with GC cycle logs on our side, so some of it could be client side.
[02:51] Santiago: okay, couple of things to call out: 1) we have session pinning that can reduce reloading, 2) you can pre-warm the kv cache using a small synthetic prefix workload we can provide, and 3) quantization profile can affect tail latency; int8 tends to improve throughput but sometimes increases per-token variance on certain ops.
[03:15] Priya: you mentioned fallback policies earlier — under Dedicated shortage would requests route to hosted? what's the SLO there?
[03:26] Santiago: yes, we can route by policy. typical rollforward is: prefer dedicated, fallback to cheaper hosted variant or a lower-seq-length variant. SLO depends on the pool — hosted has a slightly higher p99 in our org benchmarks but we can set soft timeouts and hedging. i'll outline options in the rollforward doc.
[03:45] Marcus: for compliance, if a fallback routes to hosted does that break data residency? we need to avoid that.
[03:55] Maya: good flag — you can configure routing policies by tag; we can ensure any requests with residency tag never leave the private pool. the fallback would be only for non-sensitive traffic.
[04:10] Tom: on the bench itself we also saw a weird pattern where throughput dropped for 4 min blocks; the server logs show a backoff/retry loop.
[04:20] Eliot: that could be our autoscaler transiently rebalancing GPUs — did you run the test with sustained qps or bursty arrivals?
[04:30] Ava: sustained at ~120 rps, about 20 concurrent sessions.
[04:36] Maya: sustained 120 rps should be fine for the dedicated shape you requested; the drop suggests either a drain event or a cache eviction. can you share the trace ids?
[04:46] Tom: yes i'll upload traces.
[04:49] Santiago: let's walk through a short debugging checklist — kv cache warm-up, batch sizing, seq_length clamps, and fallback route tags. i'll go through each quickly.
[05:02] Maya: kv cache warm-up: run the synthetic prefix with roughly 10% traffic to warm top-of-stack embeddings and kv slices; that usually removes the first-wave p99s.
[05:15] Santiago: batching: we recommend starting with continuous batching enabled and a max_batch_latency of 20ms for low-latency workloads; raising it to 30-40ms can improve throughput at the expense of extra tail.
[05:29] Eli: our infra prefers lower jitter so 20ms is fine; we'll test 25ms too.
[05:33] Priya: seq_length clamps? you mean truncating to a max token window at the gateway?
[05:38] Maya: yes, enforce a soft clamp of 1024 for this experiment; long tails caused by 1.8k+ sequences accounted for a lot of token cost and caused kv thrash.
[05:49] Tom: will truncation change model responses materially? our product team is sensitive to accuracy.
[05:55] Santiago: it's a tradeoff — you can do progressive truncation (drop older context first) and compare evals; we can run a small qual eval to measure delta.
[06:05] Marcus: about security, Priya had a question on audit logs and retention. Priya?
[06:10] Priya: yes, we need audit logs for all token-level requests for 90 days. do you support that level of retention in staging and private?
[06:20] Maya: staging can hold 30 days by default; private deploy supports 90+ with log-forwarding to your SIEM. for hosted we can forward to your cloud logging but there are retention costs.
[06:34] Priya: okay we'll want private-level retention for sensitive endpoints. i'll mark which routes are sensitive.
[06:42] Santiago: perfect. next, rollforward contingency: I propose a three-tier plan — primary dedicate, secondary private-hosted pair (hosted variant with residency tag disabled only for non-sensitive), tertiary rate-limit degrade band for lightweight responses.
[06:58] Ava: sounds good. can you define the degrade band? like what does "lightweight responses" mean?
[07:05] Maya: typically respond with a trimmed summary of source plus explicit confidence and a link to re-run when full model available; reduces token cost by ~60% and latency by ~40%.
[07:18] Tom: ok. tactical: for the immediate next bench we want to test warm-up vs no warm-up and compare p99 stability. can we get the warm-up script?
[07:27] Santiago: yes, i'll attach it. it's a small harness that issues synthetic prefixes and keeps kv warmed. also includes a small python snippet to prime the cache across the pool.
[07:36] Eliot: can that be run as a k8s job? our infra prefers that.
[07:40] Maya: we provide a dockerized version. we'll send the k8s job manifest so you can schedule as a cron.
[07:47] Marcus: on traces — in the logs we saw some token accounting mismatch where the reported tokens didn't match our client-side tokeniser; any thoughts?
[07:57] Maya: tokenisation differences happen — we support multiple tokenisers and we can surface the exact encoding. recommend using our tokenizer util to match token counts. we'll attach that util.
[08:10] Tom: also saw a few 429s from the gateway during the 10k run — looks like short-lived rate limit bursts.
[08:18] Santiago: that might be a per-token throttle kicking in; the staging defaults are conservative. we'll increase the per-client token rate for your staging project.
[08:29] Priya: about SSO — does Redwood support SAML with Okta? we need SCIM groups synced for role mapping.
[08:38] Maya: yes, SAML + SCIM supported; we'll send the IdP config and example attribute map. for now staging uses invite-based accounts.
[08:48] Ava: timeline question: if we complete the bench this week and accept the extent of p99 work, when could we move to an initial canary with 5% production traffic?
[08:58] Santiago: if bench is clean and quant profile documented, we can schedule a 5% canary within two weeks — so roughly mid-March. that assumes no blockers on SSO/KMS.
[09:11] Marcus: we also need cost projections for int8 vs float16 variants.
[09:18] Maya: we'll model that — int8 typically reduces GPU memory and cost per token by ~30-45% depending on workload; we'll send an apples-to-apples cost delta with expected latency impacts.
[09:32] Tom: quick question on model variants: can you set the routing to a "lower-context" variant automatically when the pool is under pressure?
[09:42] Santiago: yes, routing policies can target model tags and context-length-limited variants. we'll show an example where requests above N tokens are routed to a budget model.
[09:52] Ava: great. ok, let's walk through a short set of troubleshooting items — i'll share the 4 logs we pulled.
[10:00] [screen share noise]
[10:10] Tom: here are the p95/p99 plots — you can see p99 spikes at roughly 03:12 and 07:45 during the 10k run.
[10:22] Maya: do we have correlating redis evictions or pod restart events?
[10:28] Tom: we have one pod drain event at 07:44 initiated by autoscaler due to a quota threshold; not sure why quota triggered.
[10:36] Eliot: autoscaler could scale down on ephemeral metrics; check your bucketed metric window, sometimes short windows cause oscillation.
[10:44] Marcus: we'll increase cooldown windows.
[10:47] Priya: can Redwood instrument autoscaler traces with request ids?
[10:53] Santiago: yes, we can include trace metadata with autoscaler events so you can map request ids to container lifecycle events. we'll add that to the debug artifact set.
[11:05] Ava: on the bench we also toggled continuous batching and saw 12% lower cost but p99 increased slightly — that lines up with what you said.
[11:15] Maya: continuous batching buys token-level cost efficiencies; for chat interactive apps you need to tune max batch latency carefully.
[11:24] Tom: another small oddity — one of our clients uses a websocket-based connector and saw an extra 40ms overhead; any tips?
[11:33] Maya: websocket proxying and per-message ack can add latency; consider a pooled connection approach or set a keepalive that avoids frequent reconnects.
[11:42] Marcus: final question for roadmap: if we move to private deployment down the road what is the migration lift from dedicated?
[11:51] Santiago: migration is straightforward — the API surface stays the same. main lift is networking (vnets/VPC peering, KMS integration) and we provide an ops runbook and optional runbook assistance. timeline typical 6-8 weeks for initial private deployment depending on compliance gating.
[12:08] Priya: who is our primary contact for the KMS handshake?
[12:12] Santiago: Maya will lead that.
[12:15] Maya: happy to. i'll loop in our security PM for the handshake.
[12:20] Tom: back to rollforward — do you have a canned communication template for failover to inform product and users?
[12:28] Santiago: yes, we have a template for user-facing degrade notices and internal runbooks. i'll include both in the playbook.
[12:35] Ava: good. let's confirm immediate next steps and owners.
[12:40] Santiago: recap: redwood provides staging gateway creds packet and warm-up script by 3/4; customer runs 10k bench with warm-up and without and uploads traces by 3/8; redwood sends quant profile and cost delta by 3/9; security doc exchange targeted 3/11.
[12:59] Marcus: sounds good. any blockers from customer side?
[13:03] Ava: none besides scheduling some infra time.
[13:06] Priya: we'll start collating compliance items.
[13:10] Santiago: awesome. are there any lingering questions?
[13:15] Tom: none from me.
[13:17] Maya: i'll follow up with the k8s job manifest and the tokenizer util.
[13:23] Santiago: thank you everyone — we'll send the packet and the rollforward doc this afternoon. talk soon.
[13:30] [meeting ends]

Notes on errors/typos: occasional transcription errors with product names ("kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cache"), and speaker labels occasionally generic; logs and links referenced are in shared drive rather than embedded in transcript.
